description: A creative and technology-driven team skilled in coding, software, hardware, game development, web development, graphic design, animation, and data analysis. Passionate about planets, moons, Mars, satellites, and space exploration, we combine engineering and creativity to build innovative simulations and solutions for real-world challenges.
summary:
We developed Lunar Outpost – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, an interactive 3D educational game that simulates life on the Moon. Players take the role of astronauts and mission commanders, building and managing their own lunar base. The game includes a dome habitat, garage, mission office, solar panels, greenhouse, rocket, exploration rover, communication dish and astronaut systems. Players can explore the lunar surface, manage resources, maintain equipment and operate different mission facilities.
Our project addresses the challenge by providing a hands-on simulation that teaches players what it takes to establish and sustain a lunar outpost. Players must manage oxygen, water, food and electricity while responding to emergencies such as equipment failures and oxygen leaks. They make important engineering decisions, explore the Moon and balance limited resources. We also aim to integrate real NASA datasets to make the experience scientifically authentic.

Living on the Moon is one of humanity's major future challenges. Our project helps young explorers understand the science, engineering and teamwork required for sustainable space exploration. It encourages problem-solving, critical thinking and environmental awareness through interactive gameplay. Most importantly, it transforms complex space science into an engaging learning experience and inspires the next generation of scientists, engineers and astronauts.

It can be played through windows OS and through the web browser
details:
Lunar Outpost – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

What does it do and how does it work?

Lunar Outpost is an interactive 3D simulation game that allows players to experience life as astronauts on the Moon. Players can explore the lunar surface, build and manage a lunar base, operate vehicles and maintain essential facilities. The simulation includes solar power generation, greenhouse farming, oxygen, water and food management, equipment maintenance, rocket operations and lunar exploration. Players must make decisions and balance limited resources to keep their crew safe and their mission operational.

What benefits does it have?

The project makes complex space science easier and more enjoyable to understand. It teaches resource management, engineering, sustainability, problem-solving and decision-making through interactive gameplay. It also introduces players to the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence beyond Earth.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and astronauts by making space exploration accessible and educational. We want players to understand the real challenges of living on the Moon and the importance of sustainable systems for future space missions.

What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

We used the Godot game engine to develop the 3D simulation, Blender for 3D modelling and asset preparation, and GLB 3D models for the lunar base, vehicles, astronaut equipment and other facilities. We also aim to incorporate NASA open datasets, including DONKI space-weather data, OSDR space-biology data and Artemis-related information, to improve scientific authenticity.

How is your project creative?

Instead of simply showing information about the Moon, our project turns lunar exploration into an interactive mission. Players become base commanders who must make real engineering decisions, manage interconnected systems, respond to emergencies and explore the lunar environment. This combination of gaming, education and space science makes learning more immersive.

What factors did your team consider?

We considered scientific accuracy, limited resources, astronaut safety, power generation, life-support requirements, sustainability, accessibility and age-appropriate gameplay. We also focused on creating an engaging and replayable experience that introduces important scientific concepts without overwhelming young players.
